newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIUM'S TRAGEDY: A RICH PEOPLE, BUT A ROUTED STATE.
newsitem.headline: BELGIUM'S TRAGEDY: A RICH PEOPLE, BUT A ROUTED STATE.

text.p: Belgium's tragegy is that all the wealth is concentrated in the hands of families, while the debt is concentrated in the hands of the state, Belgian central bank governor Alfons Verplaetse said.
He was speaking at the presentation of the bank's annual report on Wednesday. His comments were embargoed for Friday.
Families' net financial assets amounted to 16,836 billion francs at the end of 1995, when the state's net debt totalled 9,520 billion. It rose to 9,528 billion at the end of 1996.
Families' high savings rates led them to build up net financial assets worth about 210 percent of Gross Domestic Product (GDP) at the end of 1995.
